references.text: The Lord describes Israel as a stiff-necked people (עַם־קְשֵׁה־עֹרֶף), the same expression used here in 33:5
Shortly before this verse, the Lord warns that he may consume the people on the way because they are stiff-necked
Moses asks the Lord to go with them even though they are a stiff-necked people
Moses reminds the people that they are a stiff-necked people, the same characterization used by the Lord
The Lord repeats the description of Israel as a stiff-necked people
Moses exhorts the people not to be stiff-necked any longer
Stephen uses the term σκληροτράχηλοι (stiff-necked) about the Jews, reflecting the Hebrew עַם־קְשֵׁה־עֹרֶף
The Lord threatens to consume the people (וַאֲכַלֵּם), parallel to the threat וְכִלִּיתִיךָ in 33:5
The Lord threatens to consume the congregation in an instant, a similar threat as in 33:5
The Lord again threatens to consume the congregation in an instant
The people remove their jewelry in response to the Lord's words, a direct fulfillment of the command in verse 5
The people removed their jewelry at Mount Horeb, continuing the command given in verse 5
Prophetic precursor: The characterization 'stiff-necked' in 33:5 anticipates and illuminates the future idolatry described in 31:16.
Cause and effect: 32:7 describes the sin that directly leads to the characterization and judgment in 33:5.
